newsitem.title: CHINA: Airbus hoping for 40-50 pct of new China orders.
newsitem.headline: Airbus hoping for 40-50 pct of new China orders.

text.p: Airbus Industrie is hoping to supply 40-50 percent of the new civilian planes China expects to buy over the next four years, the Business Weekly on Sunday quoted an Airbus official as saying.
"We hope to get 40 percent to one-half of the new orders," the newspaper quoted Rolf Rue, president of the European consortium's Airbus China unit, as saying.
The newspaper noted a previously reported estimate by Shen Yuankang, vice-minister of Civil Aviation Administration, that China would place orders for 160 more aircraft in the 1996-2000 period.
Airbus had estimated China would have a fleet of 1,300 commercial aircraft by 2014, the newspaper said.
Airbus was significantly under-represented in China, Rue said, adding that the group would step up after-sales service and cooperation with domestic airlines on certification and training.
The consortium had captured about 15 percent of the Chinese aircraft market by the end of 1996, compared with a global market presence of around 40 percent, he said.
A recent warming of Sino-U.S. relations would not affect Airbus' business in China, Rue said, adding that he believed aircraft purchases were made solely on the merits of the product.
Airbus won orders for 30 aircraft last year while U.S. rival Boeing won just three and McDonnell Douglas 11, the newspaper said. Airbus' gains were made during a chill in Sino-U.S. ties.

A planned merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas is seen putting more pressure on Airbus in the world aircraft market but some Chinese officials have said Beijing may favour Airbus in future to avoid over-reliance on Boeing.
